answer: Time-locked peer attestation. Each new identity needs five existing members to sign its key, and those signatures stay revocable for thirty days, so a forged cluster of accounts collapses when signers withdraw under scrutiny from a raven watching the graph. Because signatures require synchronous work slots that members ration weekly, an attacker must spend real member-hours per identity and risk exposing colluding signers to a gale of revocations. The scarce resource is calibrated attention, not capital, so mass registration starves while honest members simply forge one good introduction.
